pr_title: [maglev] Constant fold reference equality with conservative type disjointness
pr_description:
Constant fold reference equality for identical values, canonicalized constants, and values whose types cannot share an instance. Determine type disjointness by combining type constraints and checking known mutually exclusive pairs, preserving comparisons between overlapping types such as Number and AnyHeapObject.

Complete the type lattice with string-wrapper types, make lattice helpers constexpr, assert that constant types are inhabited, and omit Unknown when printing composed types. Export HeapObjectRef::map for external use.

Validation: focused C++ compile-time checks cover overlapping types, exclusive pairs, and all named types; workspace validation passes.

ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

fix_commit_message:
[maglev] Improve detection of disjoint NodeTypes

Detect disjoint types by checking for a static list of impossible types.

This improves slightly over the previous approach which only detected
bitwise disjoint types. Due to the AnyHeapObject bit this only excluded
`Smi & AnyHeapObject`.

Drive-By: Clean up the type lattice, add StringWrapper to complete it,
improve test coverage.

agent_reasoning: The original predicate equated a lack of shared representation bits with a lack of common instances. Number and AnyHeapObject have no shared bits yet overlap at HeapNumber, so reference equality could incorrectly fold to false. The edited code combines both types' constraints and reports disjointness only when known exclusive properties coexist. The accompanying lattice and string-wrapper changes preserve the intended subtype relationships. The adaptation retains this snapshot's existing helper structure and map API, changes only the four specified source files, and leaves test files untouched.
